samples.summary: `allSamplesFailedError`'s documented multi-sample selection (`list.find`, not `list[0]`) has no test — every new test passes a single-element results array
samples.evidence: The extracted function's docstring makes an explicit behavioral claim: "The FIRST such sample wins, not the first sample overall: with N samples a transient outage can hit only some of them" (review-panel.mjs:1763-1765), and the message is separately taken from `list[0].__error` (line 1769). Every test that exercises it passes a one-element array: `synthesisedRecord([drainedPoolSample()])`, `synthesisedRecord([ranButProducedNothing])`, `synthesisedRecord([{__error:..., kind:"no-output"}])` (prior-findings.test.mjs:329, 350, 356). No test passes e.g. `[{kind:"no-output", __error:"A"}, drainedPoolSample()]` to pin that (a) the never-ran sample is found at a non-zero index and still sets `infra`/`kind`/`code`/`reason`, and (b) `err.message` still comes from sample 0. Replacing `list.find(sessionNeverRan)` with `list[0].kind === ...` — or with `results.find(r => r.kind === "api-error")`, the exact pre-fix predicate — would keep the whole suite green while re-introducing the same class of misclassification the PR fixes (a partially-failing multi-sample lens published as a blocking code finding). The PR's own rationale is that this branch "was the one branch with no test"; the multi-sample half of it still is. Nothing else covers it: no other file constructs multi-sample results for this function.

samples.summary: The "producer to consumer" round-trip tests still hand-mirror two of the three links (the panel's `failFindings` shape and `runSample`'s error projection), so the chain they claim to pin can break with the suite green
samples.evidence: The helper's own docstring warns that "a fixture hand-written to look like the producer's output would keep passing after the producer stopped emitting it", then does exactly that for two links: `synthesisedRecord` restates `{ severity: "major", summary, ...(err.infra ? { infra: true } : {}) }` (prior-findings.test.mjs:20-21) instead of calling the real producer at review-panel.mjs:2839, and `drainedPoolSample()` (lines 26-30) restates `runSample`'s catch projection from review-panel.mjs:2794. Consequences: if line 2839 stopped spreading `infra: true` (or renamed it), or if `runSample`'s catch stopped copying `kind` — the single field `sessionNeverRan` reads, i.e. the actual carrier of the fix — these tests still pass, because the fixture supplies both. Note also a live divergence: the real producer keys the flag on `lensInfraReason(err)` (line 2819) while the helper keys it on `err.infra`, so the helper is not the same expression it claims to mirror. Only link 3 (`tagPriorFindings`/`isInfraRecord`) is exercised against real code end to end.

samples.summary: `lensInfraReason` is not tested for the two cases that distinguish it from `lensFailureSummary`: an infra error carrying a `reason` (which it deliberately ignores) and an infra error with no `kind`
samples.evidence: `lensFailureSummary` prefers `err.reason` (review-panel.mjs:1710) while the new `lensInfraReason` always re-derives from `{kind,status,detail}` (line 1739). No test pins that asymmetry: redact.test.mjs:344-358 uses a bare error with no `reason`, and 361-372 covers only null cases plus `{infra:true,kind:"api-error",status:429}`. So the request-id-carrying case pinned for the human renderer (redact.test.mjs:329-341, "the request id was lost on the way to the PR") has no counterpart for the machine-readable `infraError`, and neither does the backward-compat claim in the comment at lines 1712-1717 that a `kind`-less error still classifies as `api-error` (that claim is only covered for `lensFailureSummary`, via redact.test.mjs:261). Either behavior could change silently.

samples.summary: The new `poolExhaustedError` test largely duplicates the existing one at ask.test.mjs:296 and omits `status`, the one projected field left unasserted
samples.evidence: ask.test.mjs:296-305 already asserts `kind`, `retryable` and the operator message for a drained pool; the new test at 787 re-asserts all three and adds `code`/`reason`/`detail`. It never asserts `status`, even though `runSample`'s projection copies `e.status` (review-panel.mjs:2794) and `safeFailure` does not set it — so the field silently travels as `undefined` where every `classifyResult` failure carries an explicit `null`. Folding the new assertions into the existing test (or adding `assert.equal(err.status, null)`) would cover the whole projected shape without the overlap.

verdict.reason: The literal absence is real — no test passes a multi-element array to `allSamplesFailedError` (only three single-element call sites at prior-findings.test.mjs:334, 366, 372; redact.test.mjs exercises the renderers via hand-built Errors, never through this function; review-panel.test.mjs never imports it). It is not blocking under the test-adequacy rubric. (a) The finding's central premise is false: reverting to the "exact pre-fix predicate" `results.find(r => r.kind === "api-error")` would NOT keep the suite green, because drainedPoolSample carries kind "pool-exhausted" (ask.mjs:634/642), so err.infra would be falsy and prior-findings.test.mjs:338 and :341 would fail. The behavior this diff changed (widened predicate + kind carried to both renderers) is genuinely pinned. (b) The untested half — `find` over all samples plus message from index 0 — is pre-existing behavior carried over verbatim from .trusted/scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:2738-2740; the extraction only documented it. (c) Every lens in scripts/agent/lenses/lenses.json is "samples": 1, so the non-zero-index case is unreachable in the shipped config. That makes this "coverage could be broader but the core behavior is tested" (minor), and the rubric forbids flagging "add more tests" as a blocker when the real behavior change has meaningful coverage.
